q: What is the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix used for?
o: Classifying generative AI use cases by how much of the model and app you own, to decide security responsibilities
e: The matrix runs from scope 1 (consumer app) to scope 5 (self-trained model). Your security responsibilities grow with each scope.

q: In the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix, which scope means building your own app on a pre-trained model accessed through an API, such as Amazon Bedrock?
e: Scope 1 is a consumer app, 2 an enterprise app, 3 a pre-trained model you build on, 4 a fine-tuned model, 5 a self-trained model.
an: RPGACE is scope 3: you build the app, and Oracle calls a pre-trained Claude model through an API without retraining it.

q: Which scope in the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix carries the most security responsibility for the customer?
e: Training your own model means you own the data, training, model, hosting and app security.

q: Which AWS service provides threat detection by analysing account activity for suspicious behaviour?
e: GuardDuty continuously monitors for malicious activity and unauthorised behaviour.

q: Which describes data retention policies for AI workloads?
o: Rules for how long data such as prompts, logs and training sets is kept and when it is deleted
e: Retention limits risk and supports compliance: keep only what you need, for as long as you need it.

q: Which practice helps secure an AI application against prompt injection? (Choose TWO.)
o: Validate and filter inputs and outputs, for example with Bedrock Guardrails
Limit the tools and permissions the model can use
Put secrets in the system prompt
e: Defence in depth: guardrails, input and output checks, separating instructions from data, and least-privilege tool access.

q: Which is a governance practice for AI systems?
o: Defining policies for approved models, data use, review and monitoring
Letting each developer choose any model without records
e: Governance sets the rules, owners, review processes and documentation for AI use.

q: How can a company enable logging of Amazon Bedrock prompts and responses for auditing?
o: Turn on Bedrock model invocation logging to CloudWatch Logs or Amazon S3
e: Model invocation logging captures request and response data for audits and analysis. Protect these logs, as they may contain sensitive data.

q: Which identity mechanism lets an application running on AWS call Bedrock without storing long-term access keys?
o: An IAM role attached to the compute resource
Hard-coded access keys in the code
A public API key in the browser
e: IAM roles give temporary credentials automatically. Never embed long-term keys in code.

q: Which AWS service protects web applications from common attacks such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting?
e: AWS WAF filters malicious web requests at the edge or load balancer.
an: RPGACE closed its own cross-site scripting gap by escaping HTML before showing Oracle's replies, so text fetched from the web can't run as code.

q: Which describes encryption in transit?
o: Protecting data while it moves between systems, for example with TLS
e: TLS encrypts data moving over networks. Encryption at rest protects stored data, often with KMS keys.

q: Why should access to a vector database used for RAG be controlled carefully?
o: It may contain sensitive company content that the model could reveal to unauthorised users
It is required to change the temperature
e: RAG can surface whatever is indexed. Enforce permissions at retrieval and index only appropriate data.

q: Which AWS service gives a central view of security alerts and compliance status across accounts?
e: Security Hub aggregates findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie and more, and checks against standards.

q: An AI agent needs to act on behalf of users and access third-party tools securely. Which Amazon Bedrock AgentCore component manages this?
e: AgentCore Identity manages agent identities and secure access to AWS resources and third-party services, including OAuth.

q: Which is a reason to keep personally identifiable information (PII) out of prompts and training data where possible?
o: It reduces the risk of the model exposing personal data and helps meet privacy laws
It is required to use GPUs
e: Minimising PII lowers privacy risk. Use redaction (Comprehend or Guardrails) when PII can't be avoided.

q: Which pairs a compliance task with the right AWS service? (Choose TWO.)
o: Audit trail of API calls: AWS CloudTrail
Download AWS's ISO certificates: AWS Artifact
Find PII in S3: Amazon Polly
e: CloudTrail logs API activity. Artifact provides AWS compliance reports. Macie finds PII, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities and Config tracks configuration.

q: What is the security benefit of a managed, serverless AI service such as Amazon Bedrock compared with self-hosting a model on EC2?
o: AWS takes on more infrastructure security work, such as patching and hosting
The customer has no security responsibilities at all
It removes the need for IAM
e: Managed services shift infrastructure duties to AWS. Customers still own data, access, application and prompt security.

q: Why should model artefacts and training datasets be versioned?
o: So you can trace which data produced which model, reproduce results and roll back
Because AWS charges less for versions
e: Versioning supports lineage, audits, reproducibility and safe rollback.

q: Which describes an AI governance board or review process?
o: A group that approves AI use cases, checks risks and sets policies
e: Organisational governance assigns accountability and reviews high-risk AI uses before launch.

q: Which data source risk should be checked before using third-party data for training?
o: Licensing terms and whether you have rights to use it for AI
e: Confirm usage rights, quality and provenance of third-party data to avoid IP and compliance issues.

q: A company has no backups of its AI application's database. Which risk does this create?
o: Permanent data loss if a mistake or failure happens
e: Backups and point-in-time recovery are basic resilience controls. Without them, one bad delete can be unrecoverable.
an: RPGACE's own known risk: Supabase Free has no backup or point-in-time recovery. That's why every destructive change gets checked first, and why this question bank also lives as files in the repo.
